title: Resistance 3
subtitle: Crossing a country after the defeat
summary: Resistance 3 is Insomniac Games' PlayStation 3 first-person shooter, released in North America on 6 September 2011. Joseph Capelli leaves his family and a hidden community to travel toward New York with scientist Fyodor Malikov. The Chimera have already devastated human civilisation, shifting the story from an organised military response toward survival and a dangerous journey. Towns and hostile landscapes become individual stops rather than parts of another victorious campaign. Capelli's reason to continue is personal, giving the war a smaller human centre even when its consequences remain enormous.
body: Resistance 3 is Insomniac Games' PlayStation 3 first-person shooter, released in North America on 6 September 2011. Joseph Capelli leaves his family and a hidden community to travel toward New York with scientist Fyodor Malikov. The Chimera have already devastated human civilisation, shifting the story from an organised military response toward survival and a dangerous journey. Towns and hostile landscapes become individual stops rather than parts of another victorious campaign. Capelli's reason to continue is personal, giving the war a smaller human centre even when its consequences remain enormous.

The weapon wheel returns, letting Capelli carry a broad selection rather than choosing only two guns. Familiar Chimeran designs sit alongside new equipment, and weapons improve through use. The player can therefore respond to an encounter by changing the tool instead of waiting to find another one. A health bar and recovery items also return, making supplies and the aftermath of a fight matter between attacks. Explosive environmental objects provide further options, turning the position of enemies and nearby hazards into part of selecting a shot.

The campaign supports cooperative play, including local split-screen, so a second player can accompany the trip through the ruined country. PlayStation Move and stereoscopic 3D were also supported, extending the ways the same adventure could be presented and controlled. Marcus Smith directed, Drew Murray led design and Boris Salchow composed the score. Reviewers generally welcomed the more focused journey and returning arsenal. The game became Insomniac's final Resistance entry, and Sony closed its online servers with those of the earlier PlayStation 3 games in April 2014.

Carry the arsenal and keep it useful
A journey that another player can share
